summary.headline: Snowman Logistics Q2 FY27 call: pallets stored up ~10% YoY, ~23,000 pallets being added, FY27 EBITDA seen crossing INR100 crore; PAT remains thin.
summary.overview: This was a joint Gateway Distriparks and Snowman Logistics Q2 FY27 call, with Snowman questions covering warehousing, 5PL, capex and margins. Management said pallets stored rose close to 10% YoY, with warehousing revenue growing about 10-11%, while utilisation held at 85% against a targeted 88-89%. 5PL grew only 1-2% as one major customer declined and another grew, and no new 5PL customer was added this fiscal. Management said Snowman is on track to cross INR100 crore EBITDA this year but gave no firm PAT trajectory, citing reinvestment-driven interest and depreciation. On the Gateway side, management guided to a 100,000 TEU-per-quarter rail-volume floor and double-digit growth for next year, with Western DFC and JNPT linkage still unproven for volume shifts.

financial_highlights.change: Flattish; one customer negative, rest positive
Analyst-cited figures, not disputed by management

segments.name: Snowman warehousing
segments.commentary: Pallets stored up close to 10% YoY; margins described as diluted by park-and-pay (under 10% margin) and build-to-suit, with management saying core cold storage margins are intact. Minimum wage, gratuity and PF changes not yet passed through due to annual contracts.

segments.name: Snowman 5PL
segments.commentary: Growth of 1-2% in Q2; no new customer added this fiscal, with a few deals near closure. Scope expanded for one major customer to pan-India; management is avoiding low or negative margin business.

segments.name: Gateway container business (CFS, ICD, rail, road)
segments.commentary: Rail volumes recovered about 11% QoQ; management targets at least 100,000 rail TEUs per quarter. Ankleshwar MMLP EXIM permissions are in place and volumes are minimal so far.

guidance_outlook: Snowman expects to cross INR100 crore EBITDA this year; PAT growth is not committed given interest and depreciation from reinvestment.
Snowman is adding close to 23,000 pallets in the next few months, with a further 20-odd thousand pallets under discussion.
Gateway: rail volume to hold around 100,000 TEUs per quarter; double-digit rail growth guided for next year, full-year FY27 uncertain after weak Q1.
Indore ICD targeted operational by December 2027, with volume contribution about 6 months after that and a 2-year ramp-up.
Jaipur ICD: court order reserved; if favourable, up to 18 months needed to be fully operational.
capex_capacity: Snowman new facilities are fully temperature-controlled with minimal dry share; existing capacity is about 10-12% dry, with three dry warehouses adjoining cold facilities.
Park-and-pay capacity was reduced when some leases ended; asset-light short-term arrangements of 10-14 months are used to flex capacity.
New projects target at least 15% IRR and a 7-year payback, per management.
Capex is a mix of replacement, shifting from leased to owned trains, and fleet electrification; no asset turnover figure was given.
Indore ICD civil and rail works are in full swing.
demand_pricing: Price increases were passed through after fuel hikes, with matching cost increases, per management.
Ankleshwar EXIM mix will lower realisation per TEU due to shorter lead distance; management says it will focus on EBITDA.
Snowman's 5PL pricing is mostly linked to customer sales, with contractual guardrails on procurement.
Power cost pass-through is applied at contract renewal, assuming 6-8% annual increases.
Loco and crew shortages at Indian Railways are seasonal, per Gateway management.

qa_highlights.question: Is Snowman's PAT likely to grow meaningfully and when does profitability improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reinvestment keeps interest and depreciation high, so PAT may grow modestly; focus is on operating cash flow and EBITDA, with Snowman on track to cross INR100 crore EBITDA this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why are warehousing margins falling over the long term?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 5PL mix, park-and-pay spot business at under 10% margin, build-to-suit at lower margin, and minimum wage, PF and gratuity changes not yet passed through. Utilisation at 85% versus a targeted 88-89% also cut margins by about 2-3%.

qa_highlights.question: How much could DFC and JNPT linkage lift Gateway volumes and EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to size; road-to-rail shift of about 10,000-15,000 TEU per month is possible, but shipping line routing decisions at JNPT are the main driver.

qa_highlights.question: Is Indian Railways likely to cut tariffs post-JNPT DFC linkage?
qa_highlights.answer: Representations have been made for tariff rationalisation to compete with Mundra and Pipavav, but management said it is too early to comment and expects incremental JNPT rail volume in a couple of months.

qa_highlights.question: What are Snowman's capex plans and how is expansion funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Expansion is through both build-to-suit and owned capacity, with about 23,000 pallets under construction and 20-odd thousand under discussion; no capex quantum was disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Jaipur ICD status?
qa_highlights.answer: All final arguments are complete and the order is reserved; if favourable, construction starts and operations take up to 18 months.

risks_watch: Snowman margin trend: warehousing margins have declined over several years, and management has not yet passed on wage and PF cost increases in annual contracts.
5PL growth is only 1-2%, with no new customers added this fiscal and one major customer declining.
Gateway JNPT rail volume uplift depends on shipping lines and tariff decisions by Indian Railways; neither is yet confirmed.
Ankleshwar EXIM ramp-up is minimal so far and will dilute realisation per TEU.
Jaipur ICD outcome depends on a reserved court order with no timeline.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously confident: management highlighted recovery and expansion plans but repeatedly declined to give numbers on PAT, JNPT volume gains, and asset turnover, and deflected some margin questions to EBITDA.
key_quotes: So PAT, like I said, because we're reinvesting, the interest and depreciation will continue to be there.
But if you look at the overall EBITDA, that's what we're focused on.
So if we talk Y-o-Y, it is close to around 10% increase in terms of number of pallets stored, not handled.
But for next year, we maintain a double-digit growth.
